children: flydubai is continuing to expand its network and add capacity as travel demand remains resilient, with the airline restoring operations to 85% of its network and now serving more than 125 destinations across 56 countries.
The Dubai-based carrier has resumed or launched services to several markets in recent months, including Aleppo, Benghazi and Bangkok.

In response to strong demand, flights to Bangkok’s Don Mueang International Airport have increased from one to three non-stop daily services, strengthening connectivity between Thailand, Dubai and destinations beyond.
The airline will further expand its network on September 23 with the launch of flights to Pokhara, its second destination in Nepal after Kathmandu.
The new route is expected to support growing flows of travel, trade and tourism between Nepal and the UAE through Dubai.

Ghaith Al Ghaith, Chief Executive Officer at flydubai, said: “The last few months have demonstrated the strength and agility of our business model and the utmost confidence we have in Dubai’s resilience. Despite the challenging operating environment, we have remained focused on restoring our network safely and efficiently, adding capacity where we see demand while opening new markets. This would not have been possible without close coordination across Dubai’s aviation and tourism ecosystem, guided by the clear vision of UAE leadership.

“We are encouraged by the confidence of our customers which is reflected in the strong performance of recently launched routes and the demand we have seen over the summer. As conditions stabilise, we remain well positioned to fully restore our network and support the growing flows of travel, trade and tourism through Dubai over the next few months.”

flydubai said forward bookings remain encouraging following the summer season, with demand expected to continue into winter. Customers are travelling to Dubai for leisure and visiting friends and relatives, while the airline is also seeing continued demand across its expanding international network.

During summer, flydubai operated 11 seasonal routes to popular leisure destinations across the Mediterranean and beyond. Bodrum, Corfu, Mykonos, Santorini and Tivat were among the destinations that proved particularly popular with UAE-based travellers and passengers connecting through Dubai.
The carrier is also increasing capacity on year-round routes, including services to Almaty, Bishkek and Tashkent.

Hamad Obaidalla, Chief Commercial Officer at flydubai, said: “We are pleased to have seen positive travel demand over the summer across our network, especially on our seasonal summer routes. To meet increased travel demand, we continue to add capacity to our year-round services, including Almaty, Bishkek and Tashkent.

“Meanwhile, Thailand remains a popular destination for both leisure and business travel, and the launch of our triple-daily service to Bangkok in November reflects growing momentum across our network and underscores our commitment to providing customers with more convenient and flexible travel options.

“We are currently operating an average of 2,200 weekly flights and aim to increase this frequency as we receive more aircraft. Our focus remains on further developing our network and supporting the full recovery of operations at DXB to pre-disruption levels.”

The combined Emirates and flydubai network remains a key driver of connectivity through Dubai, offering access to more than 214 unique destinations across more than 100 countries and generating more than 4,600 connection opportunities.

Since its expansion, flydubai has built a network spanning Africa, Central Asia, the Caucasus, Central and Southeast Europe, the GCC and Middle East, South Asia and Southeast Asia. Almost 100 of its destinations were previously underserved markets with limited or no direct connectivity to Dubai and the UAE.

The airline currently operates from both Terminal 2 and Terminal 3 at Dubai International Airport (DXB). Passengers travelling on codeshare services with Emirates can connect through Dubai’s aviation hub and access destinations across the combined network.
